ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; record the driver's failure to satisfy the NS-1 arrival/waiting prerequisites (no "I'm Here" tap, no platform arrival confirmation) in the driver's record.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the two chat messages are ordinary pickup/waiting arrangements ("At the pickup point, silver Toyota Altis", "Waited 4 min, cancelling") and the written driver statement is neutral — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Cancellation branch: cancelled_by = driver and the driver asserts a rider no-show, so NS-0 routes the case to NS-1/NS-2. NS-1 requires (i) the driver pressed "I'm Here" (or a platform auto-arrival), (ii) GPS placing the driver within the pickup radius at that moment, and (iii) more than 3 continuous minutes of waiting within range thereafter. Here (i) fails outright: F6 records no arrival confirmation at all — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null). The driver admits this in F12 ("I forgot to press the I'm Here button but I was there"), and a written statement cannot supply the missing tap — the record, not the statement, governs. The platform-arrival event in F5/F2 is a GPS-derived proximity record, not an arrival confirmation under NS-1(i), and F12 confirms no tap was made. Since NS-1 (i) is not satisfied, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be fully refunded (refund_full, $6.61, per NS-7 as a voucher).

Note on NS-2's additional flag: the extra `flag_account` attaches only where the driver DID press "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius (m_from_pickup_at_tap > 200). Here there is no tap at all (F6), so that condition is not met and no account flag is warranted; F1/F3 (34–40 m from pickup) also show he was genuinely nearby. Rider and driver profiles (F16/F17: 0 upheld disputes in 90 days) are consistent with no repeat-violation flag. RD-6 is not engaged (no route deviation in this case, no upheld dispute history).

The rider's "I was on my way down" is immaterial: the fee fails on the driver-side prerequisites regardless of the rider's conduct. Evidence is complete for every element relied on (GPS fix, timeline, fare, chat with timestamps: F11), so evidence_status = sufficient.

Amount: the entirety of the disputed item is the $6.61 cancellation fee [F4][F7]; no other charge is at issue (F8 surge 1.0×).

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's written statement that he was at the pickup point and waited is a claim; NS-1(i) requires a recorded arrival confirmation (tap or platform auto-arrival), which F6 shows never occurred. System records (timeline) override statements.
The platform 'arrival' entry is a GPS proximity record, not the arrival confirmation required by NS-1(i); F6 confirms no tap and no automatic arrival was recorded.
